title: The Nature of Prophetic Word and Divine Wrath
english: The preceding text for the clarification of Zechariah, who is the eleventh of the Twelve Prophets, having an eye of the intellect enlightened, having been made god-like by the word that came to him, saw a great vision and announced a prophetic word in many ways and in many forms. Since we are eager to understand this, let us begin with the clarification concerning him, entreating that a word may be given in the opening of the mouth, with you all running together in prayer, being confident that such a thing will be attained for the one who strives.
Zechariah 1:1: In the eighth month of the second year, during the reign of Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, the prophet, saying.

In the second year of the reign of Darius the Persian king, in the eighth month of the second year of the beginning of the one ruling, the word of the Lord came to the prophet Zechariah, declaring how a great wrath has come upon the fathers of those being reproved, with God being indignant against those being accused.

And Zechariah, to whom the word of God came, is called by the voice of the Hebrews, but to the memory of the Greeks he is being interpreted as God. For how is it not a memory of God the one who is not [missing text] of God [missing text] having? And of that same [missing text] both Berechiah is and [missing text] being named after the memory of [missing text], the father of Zechariah, [missing text] Iddo.

A tradition came to us then, to remember the bearers of prophets when they themselves also happen to be healers of God. And it is shown especially how the preceding prophet and his fathers, being of the priestly race and according to the Gospel of Luke: for the father of the Baptist John, Zechariah, and Berechiah, the parent of this one, were given these names. For as the later ones encounter the same kind as those who preceded, especially when they are saints, they possess the same callings.
And they become memories in the prefaces.

Regarding the prophecies of the ancestors called by God to prophesy and the time of their prophecy. And it is [stated] for the sake of security, so that it does not become a deception through homonymy or pseudonymity.

1.7 The word of God becomes toward someone when he participates in it, just as virtue and knowledge become in a diligent and knowledgeable man. But what the word of God implies and argues against the one established by prophetic word will be clear from the following.
1.8 'These,' he says, 'says the Lord of hosts: The Lord was angry with your fathers, a great anger' (Zechariah 1:3).

1.9 A great anger comes upon those sinning greatly and being impious; for God, giving judgment 'to each according to his works' (Romans 2:6) and according to the practice of the one transgressing the divine laws, does not threaten the same punishment to all, but [one] proportionate and corresponding to those who have sinned. And the threat breathes much goodness; for if God were to punish defensively those cast into this, he would not foretell, but would bring the punishment upon them without delay.

1.10 The possessor of the divine word stands as a protector to urge the captured toward repentance, saying: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts: Turn to me,' keeping my commandments and coming to know my truth; for thus you will find me having turned to you. For I, being unmoved and unchangeable, always being the same and likewise, seem to turn away from you and to distance myself from you when you endure this.

1.11 He speaks, indeed, to those being reproved as to one to all: 'Because you know, I will cast you away and I will cast you away from serving me; remember the law of your God, and I will remember your children.' And regarding certain sensible things such a thing appears; for the earth, while being motionless upon its own seat, those departing from it by ships, they themselves, distancing themselves, receive the sensation as if it were distancing.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
